text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE

- About 18 people were injured, some seriously, by gunfire during a rally held by President Sali Berisha in the southern town of Lushnje. The paper says 10 of Berisha's republican guardsmen were taken hostages.
- The Democratic Party and Socialist Party will end their noisy electoral campaigns in Tirana's main Skanderbeg Square where they hope to draw enthusiastic crowds.
- Overseas observers are expected to monitor some 3,000 polling stations during June 29 elections.
- The paper alleges dozens of Intelligence Service (Shik) officers and their families were seen at the airport leaving the country ahead of Sunday's elections.
- If President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party wins the elections, we will start a war to oust him by force, the "Committee of Public Salvation" in Vlore said.

- Rrapush Xhaferri, manager of the collapsed Xhaferri pyramid investment scheme, says more than twice the amount of savings that thousands of investors had deposited in his foundation, not 52 percent as had been reported.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- OSCE envoy Franz Vranitzky has convinced President Sali Berisha that polling in Albania's snap general elections should close at 6 p.m.
- Gangs clashed near a sports palace where an electoral rally was taking place. A passer-by was wounded and died later. Italian troops evacuated politicians and participants safely.
- The Democratic Party said South Albania is "forbidden fruit" for their campaign and their leaders have been beaten and activists threatened there. They called on the OSCE to check the situation.
- Socialist Party public affairs secretary Pandeli Majko said the party is sure to win in 30 of 115 constituencies in Sunday's parliamentary election.
- The U.S. commission for Security and Cooperation in Europe called on Albanians to take part in Sunday's elections and avoid violence.
- Three Democratic Party activists died and another was wounded after a car exploded in the southwestern town of Fier.

- A former chairman of the ethnic Greek Omonia organisation has been kidnapped in the southern region of Gjirokaster. His daughter, running for the parliament, called her father's abduction a political act.
- The Albanian government has used two million dollars from a reserve fund to buy urgently-needed 10,000 tonnes of wheat.
ALBANIA
- The Democratic Party has vowed it would stick to a pact signed in Rome to stage fair elections.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- The Democratic Party accuses what it terms gangs of Socialist Party chairman Fatos Nano for shooting at a Democratic rally in the southern town of Lushnje.
- The Democratic Party called on the OSCE to assess the situation in southern Albania where they charge the Socialists have wiped out political competition and speak with the language of armed bands.
- U.S. Secretary of State Madaleine Albright has called on Albanians to take part in Sunday's election and keep up the process of reconciliation.
INDIPENDENT
- An editorial says the election is being held in a tense situation and that the mandate of next parliament and government will be shortlived.
- Democratic Party leaders say elections cannot be free and fair in the south as long as Democrats are not allowed to campaign there.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- The Socialist Party has had successful electoral rallies in Mallakaster and Durres where thousands of people turned out to show their support.
- The paper publishes the electoral programme of the Socialist Party, which vows to re-establish order and integrate the country within European institutions.
